variants.text: The herder's cup: bitter root split on stone, soured in a pit, taken alone at dawn as always.
Bitter and black, brewed as it always has been, one cup taken alone on the ridge.
Split on stone, soured in a pit, poured black from iron — one highland cup, made as always.
One herder, one iron cup, the bitter root his people have always brewed at frost.
Cold on the ridge before dawn, a black bitter root, from iron as always, drunk alone.
On the highland it's bitter root, black in iron, taken alone at dawn the way it always was.
As always, the herder splits root on stone, sours it in a pit, drinks it black and alone.
Bitter root, cold ridge, iron cup. One herder at dawn, the silence, and a brew made as always.
Steeped bitter, drunk black from an iron cup, alone on the ridge as it always has been.
Only the herder, the frost, a bitter black cup poured from iron the way it always was.
Split on cold stone at first frost, soured deep in the pit — one bitter cup, always.
The highland way, always: bitter root split on stone, drunk black and alone before frost lifts.
One cup, one herder, one ridge at dawn: bitter, black, and brewed as it always has been.
Poured black from cold iron, bitter as the root it comes from, taken alone as always.
As ever, the herder brews it bitter on the ridge, black in iron, drunk alone in silence.
A bitter black root off the cold highland, split on stone, taken alone as it always has.

Bitter, black, yours alone: root split on stone, soured in a pit, drunk at dawn as always.
The herder makes it on the ridge as always — bitter root, black in iron, and the silence.
At first frost, one iron cup, bitter and black — the herder alone, as always, on the highland.
The settlement's oldest brew, dug from buried jars and passed hand to hand around the fire.
Made the old way in this settlement, poured heavy from clay and passed cup to cup.
Dug from a buried jar, kept by the fire, one brew the settlement drinks.
This is the old brew — dug up, poured by the fire, handed from one to the next.
Heavy clay cups by the embers, the settlement's oldest drink passed hand to hand.
Fill a heavy clay cup, dig it from the old buried jar, pass it around the fire.
Buried jars. Heavy clay. The settlement's oldest brew, passed from one hand to the next.
The oldest drink the settlement makes — dug up, poured heavy, taken cup to cup by the fire.
Passed hand to hand since the settlement's first day, heavy in clay, dug from the buried jar.
A brew this old is the settlement's — dug up, poured into heavy clay, and passed on.

The settlement's first brew, dug from buried jars, poured heavy into clay for all.

Poured heavy, drunk from clay, dug from the settlement's oldest buried jar and passed all around.
Every hand at the fire takes the settlement's old brew, heavy in clay, dug from buried jars.

One old brew, dug up and poured for the settlement, cup after heavy clay cup.
A young maker reinvented this one last summer — a bright flower, steeped quick for friends.
Reinvented last summer by a young maker: a bright flower, quick in the cup, poured for friends.
Warm summer nights, good friends, and a bright flower a young maker steeps quick.
This is the cup a young maker reinvented last summer — bright, quick, made for friends.

One family has poured this at dusk for lifetimes — smooth in thin porcelain, sipped apart.
A quiet pour at dusk, kept by one family for lifetimes, and mostly taken apart.

Dark seed crushed fresh in steel drums, poured into blunt metal, drunk solo.

Pale root, steeped slow and clear, the same for generations — a cup for you or one other.

A light leaf, weighed out and briefly steeped, poured into one stemmed glass for yourself.
Weigh the leaf light, steep it briefly, and keep the single glass entirely to yourself.

Made simple and poured rough, with plenty in every mug for the whole crowd.
